questions.question: Which of the following countries is completely landlocked and shares an open border with India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nepal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Nepal** is a landlocked country located in South Asia. It is bordered by India to the south, east, and west, and by China (Tibet Autonomous Region) to the north.
 
• It shares an open and porous border with India, extending over **1,751 kilometers** across the states of Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Sikkim.
 
• Nepal is completely landlocked, meaning it does not have direct access to the sea.
 
• The Indo-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship (1950) allows citizens of both countries to travel and work across the borders without requiring a visa or passport.
 
• Nepal's strategic location in the Himalayan region makes it an important neighbor to India, both culturally and geopolitically.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Landlocked Countries:**

 
 
• A landlocked country is one that is entirely surrounded by land or has coastlines on closed seas.
 
• Nepal is one of the 44 landlocked countries in the world.
 
• Other landlocked countries in South Asia include Bhutan.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Nepal Relations:**
 
 
• India and Nepal have deep historical, cultural, religious, and economic ties.
 
• Both countries share open borders, which facilitate trade and the movement of people.
 
• India is Nepal's largest trade partner and source of foreign investment.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Significance of Nepal:**
 
 
• Nepal is home to eight of the world’s ten highest peaks, including Mount Everest, the highest point on Earth.
 
• The country lies in the Himalayan mountain range, which forms a natural barrier between the Indian subcontinent and the Tibetan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Border Management:**
 
 
• The open border system between India and Nepal has both advantages and challenges, including issues related to security and illegal activities.
 
• Both countries are working on improving border infrastructure and security while maintaining the spirit of free movement.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of Carnatic style composition?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Chaturang**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chaturang** is not a part of the **Carnatic style of composition**.
 
• It is a unique form of composition in the **Hindustani classical music tradition**.
 
• The term "Chaturang" translates to "**four colors**" or "**four aspects**," representing its structure, which includes four distinct components - **lyrics, sargam (solfege), tarana, and rhythmic patterns.**
 
• Chaturang is often composed to showcase the **richness and diversity** of Hindustani music.
 
• Unlike Carnatic music compositions, Chaturang does not follow the framework of **Pallavi, Anupallavi, and Charanam**, which are integral to Carnatic music.
 
• This distinction clearly separates **Chaturang** from the Carnatic style.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Varnam**__

 __
 
• **Varnam** is a fundamental composition in **Carnatic music** and is often used as a **warm-up piece** for vocalists and instrumentalists.
 
• It combines intricate **melodic patterns** with rhythmic variations.
 
• Varnams are performed at the beginning of a concert and serve as an ideal demonstration of a **raga’s structure and essence.**
 
 
 
• **Pallavi**__
 __
 
• The **Pallavi** is the opening section of a Carnatic composition and acts as the **main theme**.
 
• It is repeated multiple times during a performance and forms the **foundation** for improvisation.
 
• It is a distinctive feature of **Carnatic music compositions.**
 
 
 
• **Ragamalika**__
 
 
• **Ragamalika** translates to "**garland of ragas**" and is a type of composition in **Carnatic music**.
 
• It involves the use of multiple **ragas** within a single composition.
 
• Ragamalikas are often used to demonstrate the **composer’s creativity** and ability to transition smoothly between ragas.

questions.question: In January 2025, Wing Commander Akshay Saxena received the Vayu Sena Medal for his role in anti-piracy operations conducted in which of the following regions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arabian Sea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Arabian Sea** is a part of the northern Indian Ocean, bounded by the Indian subcontinent on the east, the Arabian Peninsula on the west, and the Horn of Africa on the southwest.
 
• The region is a crucial route for **global maritime trade** and is often prone to **piracy activities**, especially near the Gulf of Aden and Somali waters.
 
• The Indian Navy plays a significant role in ensuring the **security of maritime trade routes** in this area, conducting regular **anti-piracy operations** to safeguard international shipping.
 
• **Wing Commander Akshay Saxena** played a pivotal role in these operations, contributing to the safety and security of maritime activities in the Arabian Sea.
 
• Due to its strategic importance, the Arabian Sea has been a focus area for **international naval coalitions** combating piracy and ensuring the free movement of trade.
 
• India's proactive role in anti-piracy operations in the Arabian Sea highlights its commitment to **global maritime security**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bay of Bengal**__

 __
 
• The **Bay of Bengal** is the northeastern part of the Indian Ocean, bordered by India and Sri Lanka to the west, Bangladesh to the north, and Myanmar and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to the east.
 
• It is primarily known for its **cyclonic activities** and is less prone to piracy compared to the Arabian Sea.
 
• The region is significant for **fishing, shipping routes, and energy exploration**.
 
 
 
• **Gulf of Thailand**__
 __
 
• The **Gulf of Thailand** is situated in Southeast Asia, bordered by Thailand, Cambodia, and Vietnam.
 
• It is primarily known for its **tourism and fishing activities**, rather than piracy-related issues.
 
• The region supports major economies in Southeast Asia through its **marine resources**.
 
 
 
• **Andaman Sea**__
 
 
• The **Andaman Sea** lies to the southeast of the Bay of Bengal and is bordered by the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Myanmar, and Thailand.
 
• It is known for **marine biodiversity** and its role as a route for regional maritime trade.
 
• While piracy is rare in this region, it is monitored for **illegal fishing and smuggling activities**.

questions.question: Which part of a Hindu temple serves as the innermost chamber for the primary deity?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Garbhagriha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Garbhagriha**, meaning "womb chamber," is the **innermost sanctum of a Hindu temple**.
 
• It is the place where the **main deity or idol** of the temple is housed and worshipped.
 
• The Garbhagriha is usually a small, dark chamber that is considered **highly sacred**.
 
• The deity housed within the Garbhagriha is regarded as the **focal point** of all temple rituals and worship.
 
• The design of the Garbhagriha often reflects a **symbolic representation** of the universe and cosmic energy.
 
• Access to the Garbhagriha is generally **restricted to priests**, emphasizing its sacred nature.
 
• It is often topped by a **Shikhara** (in North India) or a **Vimana** (in South India), which is a towering structure symbolizing a connection to the divine.
 
• In most cases, the Garbhagriha is oriented to the east, allowing the rising sun's rays to illuminate the deity during sunrise.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shikhara**__

 __
 
• The **Shikhara** is the towering spire above the Garbhagriha in North Indian temples.
 
• It symbolizes **Mount Meru**, believed to be the center of the universe in Hindu cosmology.
 
• Shikharas are often ornately decorated and serve as a **visual cue** of the temple's sacred nature.
 
 
 
• **Jagati**__
 __
 
• The **Jagati** refers to the **platform** on which the temple is built.
 
• It provides a raised base, symbolizing the **separation of the sacred space** from the mundane world.
 
• The Jagati often serves as a circumambulatory path for devotees to walk around the temple in worship.
 
 
 
• **Kalasha**__
 
 
• The **Kalasha** is a decorative, often metal finial placed at the top of the temple's Shikhara or Vimana.
 
• It represents the **symbolic pot of nectar** and is considered an auspicious element in temple architecture.
 
• The Kalasha is often associated with fertility, abundance, and divine blessings.

questions.question: The musical narration of the 'Battle of Khongjom' is a popular folk music of which State?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Manipur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Battle of Khongjom** holds significant historical importance for the state of **Manipur**.
 
• This battle was fought during the **Anglo-Manipur War of 1891**.
 
• The musical narration of the Battle of Khongjom is a prominent part of **folk music** in Manipur and serves as a tribute to the warriors who fought bravely in the war.
 
• The narration is performed in the form of traditional songs and ballads, often accompanied by **indigenous musical instruments**.
 
• The site of the battle, Khongjom, is located in the **Thoubal district** of Manipur.
 
• Khongjom Day is observed every year on **April 23rd** to honor the martyrs of the war.
 
• The rich cultural and historical significance of the Battle of Khongjom is deeply ingrained in the identity of **Manipur**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh**__

 __
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh** is known for its diverse tribal traditions and folk music.
 
• It is home to tribes like the **Adi, Apatani, Nyishi, and Monpa**, each with their unique musical traditions.
 
• The state’s music often incorporates **indigenous instruments** like the bamboo flute and drums.
 
 
 
• **Kerala**__
 __
 
• **Kerala** is famous for its classical music forms, particularly **Carnatic music.**
 
• The state also boasts rich folk traditions like **Sopana Sangeetham** and **Theyyam**.
 
• Kerala’s folk music often accompanies traditional art forms like **Kathakali and Mohiniyattam.**
 
 
 
• **Nagaland**__
 
 
• **Nagaland** is renowned for its vibrant tribal music and culture.
 
• Music is an integral part of Naga life, with instruments like the **bamboo mouth organ** and drums being widely used.
 
• The **Hornbill Festival** is a significant event showcasing the music and dance forms of various tribes.

questions.question: Which Union Territory of India has the longest coastline as per the 2022-23 Annual Report of the Ministry of Home Affairs?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Andaman and Nicobar Islands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** have the **longest coastline among all Union Territories of India**, as per the **2022-23 Annual Report of the Ministry of Home Affairs**.
 
• This Union Territory consists of approximately **836 islands, islets, and rocks**, located in the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• The total coastline of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands is around **1,962 kilometers**, making it the most extensive among all Indian Union Territories.
 
• The geographical location of these islands plays a crucial role in **India's maritime security and economy**, especially in the **Indian Ocean Region**.
 
• The islands are divided into two main groups: the **Andaman Islands** to the north and the **Nicobar Islands** to the south.
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are home to **pristine beaches**, **coral reefs**, and **dense tropical rainforests**.
 
• They are rich in **biodiversity** and are known for their **strategic importance for India's defense**.
 
• The islands are also a major tourist destination, attracting visitors for their **natural beauty** and **water-based activities**, such as diving and snorkeling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Daman and Diu**__

 __
 
• **Daman and Diu** is a former Union Territory of India, now merged with **Dadra and Nagar Haveli** to form the **Union Territory of Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu** in 2020.
 
• It has a relatively **short coastline**, located along the **Arabian Sea**.
 
• The region is known for its **Portuguese heritage**, including forts and churches.
 
 
 
• **Lakshadweep**__
 __
 
• **Lakshadweep** is the smallest Union Territory of India, consisting of **36 islands**, with only **10 inhabited**.
 
• The total coastline of Lakshadweep is around **132 kilometers**.
 
• It is famous for its **coral reefs**, **lagoon ecosystems**, and **tropical climate**.
 
 
 
• **Puducherry**__
 
 
• **Puducherry** (formerly known as Pondicherry) is a Union Territory located on the **southeastern coast of India**.
 
• It has a coastline of around **45 kilometers**, which includes popular beaches such as **Promenade Beach** and **Auroville Beach**.
 
• The region has a rich history influenced by **French colonial rule**.

questions.question: The Harsha inscription of 554 CE mentions the rise of Yajnavarman from which place?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Gaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Harsha inscription of 554 CE** mentions the rise of **Yajnavarman**, a ruler who emerged from **Gaya**.
 
• **Gaya** is an ancient city located in the state of **Bihar, India**.
 
• It is historically significant due to its association with **Buddhism**, **Hinduism**, and the presence of the **Maha Bodhi Temple**, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The city of Gaya has been a prominent religious and cultural center, well-known for its **Pind Daan rituals** performed by Hindus for their ancestors.
 
• Yajnavarman’s rise marked a political shift during the post-Gupta period, reflecting the local power dynamics in the region.
 
• The Harsha inscription provides valuable historical insight into the **regional rulers** and their contributions during the period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Thanesar**__

 __
 
• **Thanesar** is a historic town located in the state of **Haryana, India**.
 
• It was the capital of the **Pushyabhuti dynasty**, which Harsha later ruled.
 
• Thanesar was a prominent center of **political and religious activities** during the early medieval period.
 
• It is also associated with the famous ruler **Harsha Vardhana** who expanded his empire from this region.
 
 
 
• **Magadha**__
 __
 
• **Magadha** was an ancient kingdom located in what is now **Bihar, India**.
 
• It was one of the most powerful kingdoms in ancient India, and its prominence rose during the reign of the **Maurya and Gupta dynasties.**
 
• Magadha is famous for its role in the spread of **Buddhism** and **Jainism**.
 
• The region was home to cities like **Pataliputra**, which served as an important political and economic hub.
 
 
 
• **Kannauj**__
 
 
• **Kannauj** was an important city in northern India and served as the capital of several dynasties, including the **Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty**.
 
• It is located in the present-day state of **Uttar Pradesh, India**.
 
• Kannauj was known for its **rich cultural heritage**, especially its role in the production of **perfumes**.
 
• The city played a significant role in medieval Indian history, often contested by various empires for its strategic importance.

questions.question: An astronomical observation site, Jantar Mantar, which is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in which State?​
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jantar Mantar** is located in Jaipur, Rajasthan, and is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• This astronomical observation site was built by Maharaja **Sawai Jai Singh II** in the early 18th century (1727–1734).
 
• It consists of a collection of **19 architectural astronomical instruments** used for measuring time, predicting eclipses, tracking celestial objects, and determining the positions of planets and stars.
 
• The observatory houses the **world's largest stone sundial**, called the "Samrat Yantra."
 
• Jantar Mantar in Jaipur is one of the five such observatories built by Sawai Jai Singh II, but it is the largest and best-preserved among them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:**

 
 
• Jantar Mantar was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **2010** for its cultural and scientific significance.
 
• It represents an excellent example of the scientific and cultural advancements of 18th-century India.
 
 
 
• **Astronomical Instruments:**
 
 
• Key instruments at Jantar Mantar include the Samrat Yantra (sundial), Jai Prakash Yantra (hemisphere), and Ram Yantra (altitude instruments).
 
• These instruments were designed to observe astronomical phenomena with the naked eye.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, the founder of Jaipur, was a keen astronomer and mathematician.
 
• His interest in astronomy led to the construction of five observatories in Jaipur, Delhi, Ujjain, Mathura, and Varanasi, with Jaipur's being the most prominent.
 
 
 
• **Tourist Attraction:**
 
 
• Jantar Mantar in Jaipur is a popular tourist destination, attracting history and science enthusiasts from around the world.
 
• It is also used for educational purposes to teach astronomy and the history of science in India.

questions.question: "Purvang" and "Uttarang" are two sections of which of the components of Carnatic Music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Varnam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Purvang** and **Uttarang** are two integral sections of a Varnam__, a fundamental compositional form in Carnatic music.
 
• The **Purvang** (first section) typically consists of the __Pallavi, Anupallavi, and Muktayi Swaras__, while the **Uttarang** (second section) includes the __Charanam and Charana Swaras__.
 
• Varnam serves as an introductory piece in Carnatic music concerts and is used for both __performance and practice__.
 
• It is designed to showcase the raga's essence through a combination of **melodic and rhythmic elements**.
 
• Varnams are critical for improving a musician's mastery of **raga alapana, swara singing, and rhythm**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Varnam in Carnatic Music**

 
 
• It is an important compositional form in Carnatic music with both lyrical and swara-based__ segments.
 
• There are two types of Varnams: **Tana Varnam** (focused on swaras) and **Pada Varnam** (focused on lyrical content).
 
• It serves as a warm-up for vocalists and instrumentalists due to its complexity and extensive range of notes.
 
 
 
• **Pallavi, Anupallavi, and Charanam**
 __
 
• **Pallavi:** The main thematic line of the composition, repeated throughout.
 
• **Anupallavi:** A short stanza that complements the Pallavi, often elaborating on its theme.
 
• **Charanam:** The concluding section that provides variations and deeper explorations of the raga.
 
 
 
• **Role of Swaras in Varnam**
 
 
• Swara patterns in Varnam are used for strengthening control over rhythm and melody__.
 
• Muktayi Swaras and Charana Swaras are key segments that demonstrate the raga's nuances.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music Structure**
 __
 
• Carnatic music is deeply rooted in ragas__ (melodic frameworks) and __talas__ (rhythmic cycles).
 
• Compositions like Varnams, Kritis, and Tillanas serve as the foundation for its performance repertoire.

questions.question: Which Princely State was ruled personally by the Nizam and had the 'Sarf khas' estate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The princely state of **Hyderabad** was ruled by the Nizam, the hereditary monarch whose official title was "Nizam-ul-Mulk".
 
• The Nizam of Hyderabad was the **supreme authority** in the state, enjoying full autonomy under British paramountcy.
 
• The term '**Sar'khas estate**' referred to the personal domain or private estate of the Nizam, which was directly administered by him.
 
• Hyderabad was one of the largest and wealthiest princely states in India, known for its vast resources, including **rich diamond mines**.
 
• After India’s independence in 1947, the state of Hyderabad was **annexed into the Indian Union in 1948** through Operation Polo, ending the Nizam's rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Princely States in British India:**

 
 
• India had around 565 princely states before independence, ruled by local monarchs under British suzerainty.
 
• These states had internal autonomy but were bound to the British Crown in matters of defense and foreign policy.
 
 
 
• **Nizam of Hyderabad:**
 
 
• The title "Nizam" was first adopted by Asaf Jah I, the founder of the Asaf Jahi dynasty, in the early 18th century.
 
• The Nizams were known for their wealth, cultural patronage, and administration.
 
 
 
• **Operation Polo:**
 
 
• A military operation launched by the Indian government in September 1948 to annex Hyderabad into India.
 
• It marked the end of princely rule in Hyderabad and integrated it into the Indian Union.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance of Hyderabad:**
 
 
• Hyderabad was a wealthy state, with significant revenue from agriculture, trade, and industries like textiles and diamonds.
 
• The city of Hyderabad was a major center for culture, education, and architecture in southern India.

questions.question: In which state of India is the Bhil tribal community found in large numbers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Bhil tribal community is one of the largest indigenous communities in India and is primarily concentrated in **Madhya Pradesh**, followed by Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Maharashtra.
 
• Bhil tribes in Madhya Pradesh are known for their traditional art forms, including the famous **Pithora paintings**, which reflect their cultural heritage.
 
• Madhya Pradesh has a significant population of Bhils, especially in regions like the Malwa, Nimar, and Jhabua districts.
 
• The Bhil community primarily depends on agriculture, hunting, and forest produce for their livelihood and has a deep connection with nature.
 
• They are recognized as a Scheduled Tribe under the Indian Constitution, which entitles them to special benefits and protections.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhil Tribe**

 
 
• The term "Bhil" originates from the word "Billu," which means bow, as Bhils were traditionally skilled archers.
 
• They are classified as one of the **largest tribal groups in India**, with a population spread across several states.
 
• The Bhil community has its own distinct language, customs, and traditions, contributing to India's cultural diversity.
 
• They practice animism and have a rich tradition of folklore and oral storytelling.
 
 
 
• **Scheduled Tribes in India**
 
 
• Scheduled Tribes (STs) are officially designated groups under the Indian Constitution, recognized for their socio-economic disadvantages.
 
• The government provides various schemes, reservations, and welfare programs to uplift ST communities.
 
• India has a diverse tribal population, with each group having its own culture, language, and traditions.
 
 
 
• **Pithora Paintings**
 
 
• Pithora paintings are traditional murals created by Bhil and other tribal communities, depicting their beliefs and customs.
 
• These artworks are often created on the walls of houses and are considered sacred.
 
• The paintings use vibrant colors and feature themes like nature, animals, and gods.
 
 
 
• **Forest Rights Act, 2006**
 
 
• The Forest Rights Act recognizes the rights of forest-dwelling communities, including tribes like Bhils, over forest land and resources.
 
• It aims to empower tribal populations by granting them legal rights to land and forest produce.

questions.question: The Badami caves in Karnataka have been built by which of the following rulers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chalukyas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Badami Caves, located in Karnataka, were built during the reign of the **Chalukyas**, specifically under the rule of Pulakeshin I and his successors.
 
• These caves are primarily dedicated to Hindu deities like Shiva and Vishnu, along with some Jain influences, showcasing the religious diversity of the era.
 
• The rock-cut architecture of Badami caves highlights the **Dravidian style** with intricate carvings and sculptures.
 
• Badami served as the capital of the early Chalukya dynasty during the 6th to 8th centuries, symbolizing their architectural prowess.
 
• There are four main cave temples at Badami, which are a mix of **Hindu and Jain traditions**, reflecting the cultural synthesis of the Chalukya period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chalukya Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Chalukyas ruled a significant part of southern and central India between the 6th and 12th centuries.
 
• They are divided into three branches: Early Chalukyas of Badami, Later Chalukyas of Kalyani, and Eastern Chalukyas of Vengi.
 
• The dynasty was known for its patronage of art, architecture, and literature.
 
 
 
• **Rock-Cut Architecture:**
 
 
• Rock-cut temples are structures carved directly into natural rocks, showcasing advanced craftsmanship.
 
• The Badami caves are prime examples of rock-cut architecture, featuring intricate carvings and sculptures.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian Style of Architecture:**
 
 
• Originating in South India, Dravidian architecture is characterized by pyramid-shaped temples, intricate sculptures, and carvings.
 
• The Badami caves reflect early Dravidian architectural elements, which influenced later temple constructions.
 
 
 
• **Religious Significance:**
 
 
• The cave temples are dedicated to Hindu deities like Shiva and Vishnu, with Jain influences in some caves.
 
• They highlight the religious harmony and cultural synthesis during the Chalukya period.

questions.question: Dhordo, the venue of Rann Utsav (from December, 2024 to February, 2025), is located in which Indian state and near what geographical feature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gujarat – Rann of Kutch**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Dhordo is a small village located in the state of Gujarat, India, and serves as the gateway to the **Rann of Kutch**, a vast salt marsh.

• The rebellion was primarily led by the **Bhumji tribal community**, along with other tribal groups like the Santhals and Kurmis.
 
• The British East India Company’s exploitative revenue policies and increased taxes on forest produce triggered the rebellion.
 
• The Bhumji chiefs, particularly the leaders of the **Midnapore and Manbhum regions**, played a significant role in organizing the resistance.

• The rebellion was fueled by colonial interference in traditional tribal ways of life and exploitation of natural resources.
 
 
 
• **Key Leaders:**
 
 
• Prominent leaders of the rebellion included Raghunath Mahato and Durjan Singh.
 
• They mobilized tribal warriors and peasants against British forces.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• The rebellion was suppressed by the British, but it highlighted the widespread resistance to colonial policies in tribal regions.
 
• It paved the way for subsequent tribal uprisings like the Santhal Rebellion (1855–56).
 
 
 
• **Jungle Mahals:**
 
 
• The Jungle Mahals region included parts of present-day Purulia, Bankura, and Midnapore districts in West Bengal.

questions.question: Which of the following caves contain rock cut paintings dating back to the stone age era?

__
 
• The Bhimbetka Caves are a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in the Raisen district of Madhya Pradesh, India.
 
• The rock shelters of Bhimbetka contain paintings that date back to the Stone Age, specifically the Mesolithic period (c. 10,000 BCE).
 
• These paintings depict scenes from everyday life, including hunting, dancing, and communal activities, providing insights into the lives of early humans.
 
• The art includes representations of animals such as bison, tigers, and elephants, as well as human figures engaged in activities.
 
• The Bhimbetka Cave complex is one of the earliest examples of human interaction with the environment, showcasing continuity in artistic expression over thousands of years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rock Art Terminology:**

 
 
• Rock art refers to human-made markings placed on natural stone, typically in caves or open-air shelters.
 
• It includes petroglyphs (carvings) and pictographs (paintings).
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Status:**
 
 
• Bhimbetka was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2003 due to its archaeological and cultural significance.
 
• The site is noted for its unique record of human settlement and evolution over different historical periods.
 
 
 
• **Mesolithic Period:**
 
 
• The Mesolithic period, also known as the Middle Stone Age, is characterized by the transition from hunting and gathering to agriculture.
 
• Rock art from this period is significant for its depiction of social and cultural development.
 
 
 
• **Discovery of Bhimbetka:**
 
 
• The caves were first discovered by Indian archaeologist V.S. Wakankar in 1957 while surveying the Narmada Valley.
 
• Over 750 rock shelters have been identified, with around 500 containing paintings.
 
 
 
• **Comparative Sites:**
 
 
• Other significant rock art sites in India include the Adamgarh Hills (Madhya Pradesh) and the Kupgal petroglyphs (Karnataka).
 
• Globally, comparable sites include the Lascaux Caves in France and the Altamira Cave in Spain.

questions.question: In May 2025, the management of Palamu Tiger Reserve (PTR) was in talks with TRAFFIC a joint initiative between World Wildlife Fund and the International Union of Conservation of Nature to obtain a sniffer dog for____________

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Betla National Park is located in the Latehar district of Jharkhand, India, and is part of the Palamu Tiger Reserve (PTR).
 
• The park is known for its rich biodiversity, including tigers, elephants, and various other species of flora and fauna.
 
• TRAFFIC, a wildlife trade monitoring network, collaborates globally to curb illegal wildlife trade and protect endangered species.
 
• Sniffer dogs are trained to detect wildlife contraband such as tiger bones, skins, and other illegal animal products, aiding in anti-poaching efforts.
 
• Betla National Park is strategically significant due to its proximity to areas prone to wildlife trafficking, making the deployment of sniffer dogs crucial.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Palamu Tiger Reserve (PTR)**

 
 
• PTR is one of India's first tiger reserves, established under Project Tiger in 1973.
 
• It spans across the Latehar and Garhwa districts in Jharkhand and covers an area of over 1,129 square kilometers.
 
• The reserve is home to multiple species, including Bengal tigers, leopards, elephants, and sloth bears.
 
• Efforts for wildlife conservation in PTR include anti-poaching measures and habitat restoration.
 
 
 
• **TRAFFIC**
 
 
• TRAFFIC is a global wildlife trade monitoring organization founded in 1976.
 
• It is a joint program of the World Wildlife Fund (WWF) and the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).
 
• TRAFFIC works to ensure that wildlife trade does not threaten the conservation of nature.
 
• Its initiatives include training sniffer dogs, raising awareness, and collaborating with law enforcement agencies.
 
 
 
• **Role of Sniffer Dogs in Conservation**
 
 
• Sniffer dogs are trained to detect wildlife products such as ivory, rhino horns, and tiger skins.
 
• They play a crucial role in curbing illegal wildlife trade and poaching activities.
 
• Such dogs are deployed at key locations like airports, border checkpoints, and wildlife reserves.
 
• Training programs for sniffer dogs are conducted by organizations like TRAFFIC and government agencies.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity of Betla National Park**
 
 
• The park hosts diverse ecosystems, including tropical dry deciduous forests and grasslands.
 
• It is home to several endangered species like Indian bison (gaur) and giant squirrels.
 
• Betla National Park also features historical sites, including ancient forts and caves.
 
• Ecotourism initiatives in the park aim to combine conservation with sustainable tourism.

questions.question: The famous building 'Qutub Minar' has been built under which style of architecture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mamulek Style**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Qutub Minar is an iconic monument constructed under the **Mamulek (or Mamluk) style of architecture**, which is a part of the Delhi Sultanate architectural tradition.
 
• It was commissioned by **Qutb al-Din Aibak**, the founder of the Delhi Sultanate, in 1192, and later completed by his successors.
 
• This architectural style is characterized by the use of red sandstone, intricate carvings, and calligraphic inscriptions, often incorporating Islamic motifs and verses from the Quran.
 
• The Qutub Minar is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and stands at a height of **72.5 meters**, making it one of the tallest minarets in the world built of bricks.
 
• The Mamulek style of architecture often blended Islamic and indigenous Indian elements, creating a unique fusion evident in monuments like the Qutub Minar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mamulek Architecture:**

 
 
• Also known as Mamluk architecture, it emerged during the reign of the Slave Dynasty (1206–1290) in India.
 
• It extensively used locally available materials like red sandstone while incorporating Islamic architectural features such as arches, domes, and minarets.
 
• Floral patterns, arabesques, and geometric designs were a hallmark of this style.
 
 
 
• **Qutub Minar Construction:**
 
 
• Qutb al-Din Aibak began its construction, but it was completed by his successor, Iltutmish.
 
• It is surrounded by several historically significant structures, including the Iron Pillar and Alai Darwaza.
 
• The minar has five distinct storeys, each marked by projecting balconies and intricate carvings.
 
 
 
• **Delhi Sultanate Architecture:**
 
 
• It refers to the architectural developments during the rule of the Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526).
 
• It includes other notable structures like the Alai Darwaza, the tomb of Iltutmish, and the Tughlaqabad Fort.
 
• This style laid the foundation for later Mughal architecture.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:**
 
 
• The Qutub Minar complex was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1993.
 
• It is recognized for its historical, architectural, and cultural significance.

• It is widely known as the **"Queen of Hill Stations"** for its picturesque landscapes, pleasant climate, and rich flora and fauna.
 
• Ooty serves as the headquarters of the **Nilgiris District**.
 
• The hill station is situated at an altitude of approximately **2,240 meters** above sea level.
 
• It is famous for its **tea plantations**, and visitors often explore the **Tea Museum** to learn about the history and process of tea production.
 
• Popular attractions in Ooty include the **Ooty Lake, Botanical Garden, Doddabetta Peak,** and **Rose Garden**.
 
• The **Nilgiri Mountain Railway**, also known as the **Toy Train**, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a major tourist attraction in Ooty.
 
• The hill station is surrounded by lush greenery and is home to a wide variety of **flora and fauna**, making it ideal for nature lovers.

 __
